title: See what $1,000 turns into
why: Compound growth is the main engine of building wealth, and it's easier to feel than to read about.
steps: Open the calculator and enter $1,000, $50 a month, 7% a year, 10 years.
Change it to 20 years and write down both totals.
Now try $100 a month. Which change mattered more: time or money?

title: Check a horse's body condition
why: Reading a horse's weight by eye is a core skill for anyone who cares for or leases horses.
steps: At the barn, pick one horse you know well.
Look and feel along the neck, ribs, back and tailhead.
Score it 1 (very thin) to 9 (obese) and ask a barn staff member if they agree.

title: Read a sunscreen label
why: Knowing what SPF and 'broad spectrum' really mean stops you from paying for marketing.
steps: Grab any sunscreen or SPF moisturizer at home.
Read the guide and find the SPF, 'broad spectrum' and water-resistance claims on your bottle.
Note the price per ml. Would you buy it again?

title: Price a tiny business idea
why: Every business is just: what does it cost, what can you charge, and who pays.
steps: Pick one idea: herbal tea blends, playlist curation, lesson tutoring, or your own.
List what you'd need to buy and the cost per sale.
Pick a price and work out the profit on 10 sales.

title: Build one plate from the Food Guide
why: Energy for long active days comes from what's on your plate, not willpower.
steps: Open the Food Guide plate and look at the three sections.
At your next meal, build a plate that roughly matches it.
Notice your energy two hours later. Better, worse or the same?

title: Take a horse's vital signs
why: Knowing a horse's normal resting numbers helps you spot when something is wrong.
steps: With barn staff OK, count breaths for 30 seconds by watching the flank, then double it.
Find the pulse under the jaw and count for 15 seconds, then times 4.
Write both down. Ask staff what's normal for that horse.
